newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - China Steel soon may hike prices.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - China Steel soon may hike prices.

text.p: Taiwan steel product prices may rise by five to ten percent as the island's largest producer, China Steel Corp, is expected to adjust its prices on May 21, local metals traders said on Tuesday.
"China Steel plans to announce its third quarter hot and cold rolled steel prices on May 21 with a rise of five to ten percent," a Taipei base metals trader said.
China Steel officials declined to comment.
China Steel's second quarter hot and cold rolled steel prices were fixed at T$10.35 and T$13.35 per kg, respectively.
Prices for galvanised steel product, anticipating the likely China Steel hikes, had risen to between T$15 to T$17 per kg from about T$13.5 to T$16 per kg a week ago, traders said.
Traders said aluminium ingot prices fell on Tuesday to reflect higher recent import costs.

Taiwan traders have predicted local demand for basic metals would pick up slowly as the government's economic stimulus plans take effect in the construction industry, which remains Taiwan's top sector for basic metals consumption despite a long slump.
